title: Retire skills
caption: Retire skills nobody uses, so the right one stays easy to find.
analogy: Cards the dive log never mentions go into the archive box.

method.heading: Read the log
method.body: Put your skill index next to what your tasks used this season. Switch off the skills no task opened, and keep a copy with the date.
method.bodyCoding: Put the folders in .claude/skills/ next to what your tasks used this season. Move the unused ones out of .claude/skills/ into a dated archive folder the agent does not scan.
method.sub: The Episode's own method, not a published rule.
method.subCoding: The Episode's own method and folder convention, not a published rule or an app feature.

archive.heading: Archive, don't delete
archive.body: Knowledge-Centered Service archives instead of deleting: deleting can break links, and an archived article can be restored.

when.heading: When a skill is due
when.body: Anthropic: deprecate a skill whose evaluations consistently fail or whose workflow is retired.

alt.scene: The control room at night. Through the porthole, the robot hangs on its cable in the Abyss, its lamp on; the pilot sits at the console.

retire-a-skill-archive-over-delete.header: Retire a skill: archive over delete
retire-a-skill-archive-over-delete.description: Knowledge-Centered Service prefers archiving to deleting, because deleting can break links and an archived article can be restored [1]. Anthropic says to deprecate a skill whose evaluations consistently fail or whose workflow is retired [2]. Reading the dive log to pick what to archive is the Episode's own method.

read-the-log.title: Read the log
read-the-log.script: Last job: retire skills. Put your list of skills next to what your work actually used this season, the dive log on our ship, and see which skills no task ever opened.

the-archive-box.title: The archive box
the-archive-box.script: Those skills go into an archive, each with the date it was retired, so the decision is written down and nobody wonders later where a skill went.

short-index-again.title: Short index again
short-index-again.script: And the index left behind is short again, with the one you need easy to find. Remember the description buried in the middle of a stuffed manual a few Slides ago? It is back in view, and the model can pick it.
